building.name: Florida Building Code, Building
building.local_amendments_note: Technical amendments in Pinellas County are adopted countywide through the Pinellas County Construction Licensing Board (PCCLB). Its list for the 8th Edition (2023) covers definitions (substantial improvement), wind speed (1609.3), the electrical code (2701.1), coastal construction (3109.1), one City of St. Petersburg amendment to Chapter 16 (structural design), residential condensate and water piping, and plumbing section 610.2 (disinfecting water piping). None touches Chapter 29 of the Building volume or Chapter 4 of the Plumbing volume (toilet counts). The city's administrative amendments are in St. Petersburg Code Chapter 8, Article II, which could not be opened on Municode (403).

Phone: (727) 582-3011 Website: www.pcclb.com. permit.exempt_list_quote: Work Exempt from Permit. Per FBC, Section 102.2.5. The Building Official shall have the authority to determine if any casual, minor or inconsequential work is exempt from obtaining a permit pursuant to the Florida Building Code. The Building Official shall maintain a list of exempt work. [...] I. EXEMPTED PERMITS: [...] Building Permits. A building permit may not be required for the following: 1. The assembly or tie-down of prefabricated portable sheds that are less than 100 square feet [...] 2. One-story detached accessory structures used as a tool or storage shed, playhouse and a similar use serving a single family residence [...] 3. Swings and other playground equipment accessory to one or two family dwellings. [...] 4. On single family residential property, any wood, chain link, plastic or wrought iron fences [...] 5. Cement plaster (stucco) applied directly onto structures constructed of concrete masonry units. [...] 6. Decks, platforms, patios, walks and other similar flat work [...] 7. Movable cases, counters and partitions not over 10 feet in height. 8. Cabinetry, counter tops, painting, papering, tiling, carpeting and other similar finish work. This exemption is not allowed nor applicable when the work or alteration affects the structural integrity of a load bearing wall or the fire resistant material of a fire rated horizontal or vertical separation. Projects located within a designated flood zone are required to comply with the substantial improvement requirements pursuant to Land Development Regulations, Section 16.40.050 and submit a cost breakdown for any work which may be exempted from permits. 9. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets [...] 10. Temporary shade structures, tents [...] 11. Awnings for doors or windows [...] 12. Shade cloth structures constructed for nursery or agricultural purposes. 13. Interior wall or ceiling finish repair of a casual, minor or inconsequential nature in which the aggregate area of the repair does not exceed 100 square feet. [...] 14. Conversion of a garage into a temporary sales office [...] 15. Temporary buildings, sheds and trailers used exclusively for construction purposes [...]
permit.note: The List of Exempted Permits (created March 1, 2002, revised January 1, 2014) exempts 'Movable cases, counters and partitions not over 10 feet in height' (item 7) and 'Cabinetry, counter tops, painting, papering, tiling, carpeting and other similar finish work' (item 8). Toilet partitions or compartments are not named, and the list does not say whether partitions anchored to the building count as 'movable'. The plumbing list adds: 'Alterations to plumbing fixtures located within a commercial building must be compliant with Chapter 11 of the Florida Building Code and Sections 553.501-553.513'. The list's exceptions say a permit or certificate may still be required for listed items, and that work in a flood zone or a historic district may not be exempt.
permit.when_required_quote: Any owner or authorized agent who intends to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish or change the occupancy of a building or structure [...] shall file an application and obtain the required permit or certificate.

restrooms_city.note: No St. Petersburg ordinance or code amendment on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms in private buildings was found (one web search; the PCCLB amendment list has none). News reports from 2023 describe a mayor's executive policy converting single-occupancy restrooms in city-owned facilities to all-gender; it was not read on an official page and concerns the city's own buildings, so it is not in page text. The city code on Municode could not be opened, so this is 'none found', not 'none exists'.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to St. Petersburg job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for Gulf Coast humidity and see the local rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for St. Petersburg offices, schools, hospitals and waterfront restaurants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Florida's plumbing rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and St. Petersburg applies them unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** St. Petersburg's list of work that needs no building permit covers movable cases, counters and partitions up to 10 feet high, and cabinetry, counter tops, painting and tiling. It doesn't name toilet partitions or say whether partitions anchored to the building count as movable. Ask St. Petersburg Construction Services and Permitting whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: St. Petersburg Construction Services and Permitting
page.stalls_after: In restaurants and other gathering places, Florida can require three women's toilets for every two men's toilets and urinals once the men's room has more than two. Licensed restaurants may be exempt, so confirm with St. Petersburg Construction Services and Permitting. Outdoor seating counts toward the number of people. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or St. Petersburg Construction Services and Permitting sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Contractors register with St. Petersburg Construction Services and Permitting before they pull permits: a signed affidavit, a Florida or Pinellas County license and proof of insurance, plus a city business tax license if the business is based in the city. Florida has no state license category specifically for toilet partitions, and a contractor whose work falls in a licensed category needs that license, so confirm with St. Petersburg Construction Services and Permitting which one covers your job. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who pulls a permit in St. Petersburg registers a Florida or Pinellas County license with the city first.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Florida has no state wage law for public construction and doesn't let cities or school districts set one. On federally funded work the federal rate applies: $16.36 an hour plus $0.70 in benefits for a carpenter on building work in Pinellas County.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7% in St. Petersburg: 6% state and 1% Pinellas County. The county's 1% applies only to the first $5,000 of each item.
page.buyers_extra: - **Parks, marinas and beach facilities:** HDPE or phenolic for restrooms that are open to outside air and hosed down.
sources: - Codes St. Petersburg enforces: [City of St. Petersburg Construction Services & Permitting, Current Building Codes Adopted by the City of St. Petersburg (effective December 31, 2023)](https://www.stpete.org/Business/Building%20Forms%20&%20Applications/Current_Codes_Adopted.pdf), listing the 8th Edition (2023) Florida Building Code Building, Plumbing, Existing Building and Accessibility volumes, linked from the city's [Building Permits page](https://www.stpete.org/business/building_permitting/building_permits.php). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Local amendments and toilet counts: the [Pinellas County Construction Licensing Board's list of local technical amendments to the Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023)](https://www.pcclb.com/amendments.htm) has one Plumbing entry, Section 610.2 on disinfecting water piping, and none on fixture counts; the Florida Building Commission's [report of local technical amendments to the Plumbing volume](https://www.floridabuilding.org/fbc/thecode/2026_Code_Development/June_2025-1st_Comment/Local_Amendments/PLUMBING-Detail_Report-LA.docx) shows the same. Checked 2026-11-24.

- The change to the 9th Edition on December 31, 2026: Florida Building Commission, [Workplan, October 2026](https://www.floridabuilding.org/fbc/commission/FBC_1026/Commission/Workplan_October_2026.pdf). St. Petersburg had posted no notice of its own. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Work exempt from a permit in St. Petersburg: [City of St. Petersburg Building Department, List of Exempted Permits (revised January 1, 2014)](https://www.stpete.org/list_of_exempted_permits.pdf), Building Permits items 7 and 8. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Contractor registration in St. Petersburg: [City of St. Petersburg Construction Services & Permitting, Contractor Affidavit (updated July 17, 2024)](https://www.stpete.org/Business/Building%20Forms%20&%20Applications/Contractor_Affidavit.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax in Pinellas County: Florida Department of Revenue, [Form DR-15DSS, Discretionary Sales Surtax Information for Calendar Year 2026](https://floridarevenue.com/Forms_library/current/dr15dss_26.pdf) (Pinellas 1%, February 1, 1990 to December 31, 2029) and [Discretionary Sales Surtax](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/discretionary.aspx) for the $5,000 limit. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Pinellas County carpenter rate on federally funded building work: [federal wage determination FL20260222, modification 1, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/FL20260222/1). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023): Building, Plumbing and Accessibility volumes, in force since December 31, 2023 and enforced in St. Petersburg with the Pinellas County Construction Licensing Board's local technical amendments (none to the fixture counts); replaced by the 9th Edition (2026) on December 31, 2026; City of St. Petersburg List of Exempted Permits under Florida Building Code Section 102.2.5; St. Petersburg Code of Ordinances, Chapter 8, Article II (Building Code) for administrative amendments; NFPA 286 for HDPE under the International Building Code, the model for Florida's code.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of anchored toilet partitions needs a St. Petersburg permit, and whether item 7 of the List of Exempted Permits (movable partitions up to 10 feet) covers them (Construction Services and Permitting, 727-893-7231, or permits@stpete.org).

Update on December 31, 2026: the 9th Edition (2026) Florida Building Code applies. St. Petersburg had posted no notice or cut-off rule of its own by 2026-11-24 (Tampa's notice gives January 1, 2027); rewrite the 'New rules' bullet, recheck the stall table against the published 9th Edition and the city's adopted-codes list, and check the PCCLB page for 9th Edition amendments.
St. Petersburg's Code of Ordinances on Municode could not be opened: read Chapter 8, Article II once in a browser to confirm it holds only administrative amendments and no city restroom-sign rule.
The exempt list says exempt finish work in a flood zone still needs a cost breakdown, and work in a historic district may not be exempt. Not on the page; mention if a buyer asks.
News reports from 2023 describe a mayor's policy making single-occupancy restrooms in city-owned buildings all-gender; no official page was read, so it is not on the page.
The city's Building Permits page labels its codes link 'effective Dec. 2020'; the linked list itself says effective 12/31/2023 and shows the 8th Edition.

Sales tax: no Pinellas change was announced for 2027 in the Department of Revenue's November 20, 2026 notices; read the 2027 Form DR-15DSS when it is posted. The county's 1% expires December 31, 2029 unless extended.
The Department of Revenue doesn't say whether toilet partitions count as a building fixture or as goods, which decides how an installed job is taxed (same open question as Miami and Tampa).
